episode_summary: Mid-week episode on the Bitcoin Cash fork: the hosts recap the split, Coinbase's plan to support Bitcoin Cash by January 1, 2018, and the SegWit2x hard fork that was expected in November. They debate mass adoption and financial literacy, then interview Rodolfo Novak of CoinKite about the OpenDime physical bearer device, multisig, Tor-connected terminals and why Bitcoin lacks a marketing department.

cards.claim: In August 2017 the hosts explained that Bitcoin Cash split from Bitcoin after BIP 148 pushed the network to accept SegWit blocks.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Bitcoin forked. So when basically BIP 148 passed and everyone switched over to accepting Segwit blocks

cards.claim: In August 2017 the hosts said that anyone holding bitcoin at the Bitcoin Cash fork also automatically held the same amount of Bitcoin Cash.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: if you had bitcoin before this fork you also automatically have bitcoin or bcash as well in the exact same amount

cards.claim: In August 2017 the hosts said Coinbase had decided not to support Bitcoin Cash, so Coinbase customers did not get it at the fork.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: decided that says we're not even going to support bcash so if you left your money on coinbase

cards.claim: In August 2017 a Coinbase customer email said customers with bitcoin balances at the fork would have an equal quantity of Bitcoin Cash stored by Coinbase.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: customers with balances of Bitcoin at the time of the fork now have an equal quantity of Bitcoin Cash stored by Coinbase

cards.claim: In August 2017 Coinbase said it planned to support Bitcoin Cash by January 1, 2018, assuming no additional risks emerged.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: we're planning to have support for Bitcoin Cash by the 1st of January, assuming no additional risks emerge at that time

cards.claim: In August 2017 a host predicted that Bitcoin Cash would be worth close to nothing on January 1, 2018.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It's probably closer to nothing in my opinion

cards.claim: In August 2017 a host predicted that Bitcoin Cash would be nearly worthless by January 1st.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: come January 1st, your Bitcoin cash is probably going to be worth, I don't know, about as much as a hippopotamus' ass

cards.claim: In August 2017 a host said there would be a SegWit2x hard fork in November, with contention possibly causing yet another fork.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: So there's going to be a 2x hard fork, I believe, in November

cards.claim: In August 2017 a host said that Coinbase withholding Bitcoin Cash from customers would amount to stealing.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Would you consider that stealing? I would.

cards.claim: In August 2017 a host explained that Bitcoin Cash has larger blocks and does not accept SegWit transactions, while Bitcoin accepted SegWit through a soft fork.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Bitcoin Cash is larger blocks. The Bitcoin that you probably are most familiar with since you've been listening to this show is Bitcoin that now accepts SegWit.

cards.claim: In August 2017 a host argued that personal finance tools must be transparent so users understand how they work, rather than handing off responsibility for their wealth.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: we need to build tools that are transparent, allow you to have a better understanding of how

cards.claim: In August 2017 the hosts debated whether mass adoption requires users to understand Bitcoin, with one saying people using it without understanding still counts as mass adoption.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Well, it is mass adoption. They're using the thing they don't understand, right?

cards.claim: In August 2017 a host cited that roughly 70% of Americans were financially illiterate.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: if roughly 70% of Americans are financially illiterate, then that's not mass adoption on an understanding level

cards.claim: In August 2017 a host said mass adoption is not as grassroots as it seems, arguing government and private industry push it.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I don't think mass adoption is as grassroots as it seems

cards.claim: In August 2017 a host proposed that banks partner with hardware wallet makers such as Ledger so customers could hold multisig keys for their money.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Why don't we partner up with hardware wallets? And we can sell people on the idea of having a banking terminal in your house.

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak explained that to spend an OpenDime you break it, first by breaking part of the PCB and later by pulling a part with a pin.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: The first version you broke part of the PCB and the second version you stick a pin and you remove a part

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak said that a broken OpenDime exposes its private key, so the owner can sweep the funds into a wallet such as Electrum.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: now he's gonna have an open dime that's unsealed that means now the private key is visible

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak explained that OpenDime can be used as a bearer bond, with its value passed on by handing over the stick.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: You can use Open Dime as a bearer bond.

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak said CoinKite was selling thousands of OpenDime units, and that it was almost out of stock again.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: We're selling like thousands and thousands of this stuff and people are using it

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak said a technology is not massively adopted until people change their physical behavior.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: I don't think any technology is massively adopted until there's a behavior change like a physical change in people's behavior

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak said Bitcoin is underutilized, and its existing features such as multisig could support smart-contract-like uses.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: Bitcoin is so underutilized in terms of features features that it has that could be used for those smart contracts

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak predicted that big banks, which he said were slow to add new features, would eventually face their demise.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: this will also be their demise

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak said he was mostly a Bitcoin maximalist because the market did not need what other coins did.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: i don't see any need from the market for the things that other coins do right now

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak said that because Bitcoin has no marketing department, people drift to other coins for smart-contract-like features.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: because Bitcoin doesn't have a marketing department, I feel like people sort of drift to other coins for those things

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak said CoinKite's point-of-sale terminals connected back to the user's wallet through Tor.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: they actually had a way of connecting back through Tor to your wallet

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak said CoinKite shipped its terminals with a SIM card that CoinKite paid for, so they worked anywhere on Earth.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: we shipped them with a SIM card that was paid by us

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak said bulk OpenDime orders were Bitcoin-only because credit card chargebacks were a risk for merchants.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: if you want to buy bulk quantities of OpenDime, we only accept Bitcoin

cards.claim: In August 2017 Rodolfo Novak described Bitcoin in ten words as a decentralized and sensible means of free speech.
cards.speaker: Rodolfo Novak
cards.quote: Bitcoin is a decentralized and sensible means of free speech

cards.claim: In August 2017 a host said he loaded three OpenDime sticks with different amounts of Bitcoin to give to his niece.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I loaded three different amounts of Bitcoin onto them

title: TBP143 - Damned If You Do, Bored If You Don't
